assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining GLP-1 as an incretin and turning it into long-acting agonists has produced a new class of drugs for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit signals. The physiology-to-therapy arc is clear and the impact on patients is very large.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action), Mojsov (identification of the active peptide form) and Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, translation) are central. Knudsen's role is drug development in industry and the list omits other early contributors such as Habener, so any three-person configuration leaves unresolved credit.
assessment.maturity: Therapies are in wide clinical use with large randomized trials and independent replication, so the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely given the visible global impact.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers basic discovery credit over drug development; Habener is not among the credited names.
Long-term safety and durability of effects are still being accumulated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience millisecond-precise, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and has transformed circuit analysis across model organisms. It is a methodological revolution with growing, but still early, clinical translation such as retinal vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth; Miesenboeck's earlier genetically targeted photoactivation) are all decisive. Six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, so any selection excludes major contributors, notably Bamberg and Boyden.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and used for over fifteen years, so basic maturity is high. Therapeutic validation is limited, but the tool-level impact is already enormous.
uncertainties: Fair three-person allocation is hard and contested.
Fit with a medicine-oriented prize versus a tool for basic neuroscience.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells directed by chimeric antigen receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality, with approved products and expanding indications.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June led design and clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T cells with costimulatory domains; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. Original receptor-chimera concepts (e.g. Eshhar, Gross) are not among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved therapies and several years of follow-up establish efficacy in hematologic cancers. Solid-tumour success, toxicity and access remain unresolved, but recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept is outside the supplied names.
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and safety issues such as cytokine release.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new principle of intracellular signaling in which the endoplasmic reticulum reports its folding state to the nucleus. It is conceptually clear, mechanistically elegant and relevant to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently defined the IRE1-HAC1/XBP1 signalling pathway and its mechanism, including unconventional splicing. This is a compact, fair two-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Findings are conserved from yeast to mammals and have been confirmed repeatedly over three decades. Disease-linked therapeutic exploitation is still emerging, though the basic discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Contributions of other ER-stress investigators, such as Ron and Kaufman, are outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation transformed the treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor, and has spread to dystonia, other disorders and a large patient population. It is a rare example of lasting clinical effect from a neurosurgical and physiological insight.
assessment.attribution: Benabid's demonstration of thalamic and subthalamic high-frequency stimulation is the decisive clinical step. Others such as Delong and Limousin contributed to the basal-ganglia model and clinical development, but are not credited in this entry, leaving a single-laureate configuration that may under-credit them.
assessment.maturity: Used for decades with extensive randomized evidence, so well matured. The recognition is somewhat overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Single-person credit may be seen as incomplete.
Mechanism of action remains incompletely understood.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway established how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune responses, linking infection, autoimmunity, senescence and cancer immunity. It is a major conceptual advance with a growing set of therapeutic programs.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP; Barber discovered STING. Ishikawa contributed early STING work and others (Wu, Sun) were in Chen's lab, so a two-person configuration is plausible but leaves some credit questions.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is confirmed by many groups and structural studies. Clinical translation (agonists, inhibitors) is not yet proven, so maturity is moderate to high on biology and low on therapy.
uncertainties: Allocation among Chen, Barber and Ishikawa.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing led to nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a fatal childhood disease into a treatable one and validating antisense oligonucleotide medicine.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and identified the target sequence; Bennett led the development of the antisense chemistry and drug. Credit is reasonably clean, though others in the clinical program and early SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) lie outside the entry.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up, so efficacy is firm. Recognition is timely, with a platform effect still unfolding.
uncertainties: Discovery of the SMN gene itself is outside the credited names.
Whether a translational-chemistry achievement fits the committee's emphasis on discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR signaling identified a central regulator of cell growth and metabolism responding to nutrients and growth factors, with relevance to cancer, diabetes, ageing and immunosuppression.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and its role in growth control; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and the nutrient-sensing pathways. Schreiber's rapamycin-target work is also credited, and the early rapamycin discovery by others lies outside the list, so allocation is debatable.
assessment.maturity: The pathway is extensively confirmed, and rapalogs are in clinical use, though broader therapeutic promise such as in ageing has not been realized.
uncertainties: Contested allocation among Hall, Sabatini and Schreiber.
Rapamycin-target work and the early identification of the compound are distributed across several groups.
